title: Mental capacity and consent
summary: Consent to care, Mental Capacity Act assessments, best-interest decisions and the legal powers others hold (LPA, deputyship).
whenToUse: Every six months, when someone’s capacity changes, or when care is given to people who cannot consent.

statements.focus: Capacity assessments that are decision-specific, best-interest records, and copies of LPA or deputyship.
People supported to make their own choices, and the least restrictive option used.
Restrictions on liberty spotted and referred for authorisation where needed.
Mental Capacity Act training and whether carers can explain it in their own words.
Audits of consent and capacity records, and what was done about gaps.
